basis: git diff dffb673..10d27ed of abp/kit-v2 (abp.mjs, test.sh); policies.json at 10d27ed (protected paths, breakers: R3, R4, R5, R8, N1 and the tamper kind on; R6 paths in observe); git tests run here in a scratch repository. I did not run test.sh.
verdict: no pass at 10d27ed (B2 closed; B1 still open)

findings.note: checkProtected now runs in the repository the command acts on (git rev-parse --show-toplevel from the command's directory or -C), and an unknown directory refuses commit and push. Good.

findings.finding: Only the fetch route is refused. Two other ways move a remote-tracking ref without git fetch, and the push check still reads refs/remotes/*. Tested here: after 'git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/y refs/heads/dev' the push check's file list for a commit changing .claude/settings.json is empty; the same after writing the commit id into .git/refs/remotes/origin/z with a shell redirect. symbolic-ref is in no deny list; .git/refs is not a protected path, so a write there is an R6 path breach, which is observe-only (logged, not blocked). The README calls this a residual left to CI; CI only stops it if it is a required status that blocks the push to dev.
findings.fix: Either (preferred) compute the push file list against the remote's real tip from 'git ls-remote <remote> <dst>' and never read refs/remotes/* in the check; or, at least: refuse git symbolic-ref and pack-refs on refs/remotes, and make every write under .git/ (refs/, packed-refs, HEAD, worktrees/) a tamper-kind denial, like .git/config. Add tests for both routes above.

conditions_still_open: CI check wired as a required status in branch protection on dev of each repository, before any install (until then a hook bypass reaches dev unchecked).
Rotation of cl-6.abp's key through IaC.
what_would_pass: A head that closes B1 by either route above, with tests, and CI required on dev. Then I review that exact head.
